title: Risk log — Lifecycle onboarding email deliverability (Hosted API) — Sprint
content:
Last updated: 2026-02-04 (Tyler)

Purpose
- Running risk log for onboarding email v2 (lifecycle growth experiments sprint).
- Focus: deliverability + sender reputation + list health + compliance. Tracks signals (bounces/complaints), likely causes, mitigations, and owners.
- NOTE: This doc is intentionally “working”; keep updates lightweight but timely.

Primary owners / escalation
- Deliverability + sending config: Tyler Benson (MOPS) (primary), Ben Carter (backup)
- Copy / messaging changes that impact spam scoring: Soojin Lee
- Unsubscribe / preference compliance review: Michael Grant (CAN-SPAM), Olga Petrov (GDPR)
- Trigger logic / suppression / cohort flags: Ethan Park
- QA + regression checks: Leila Farouk

Guardrails (stop / slow / investigate thresholds)
- Hard bounce rate: 
  - > 1.0% on a send = investigate immediately, slow ramp until resolved
  - > 2.0% = pause expansion (no new segments) + clean list before resuming
- Spam complaint rate:
  - > 0.08% (8 per 10k) = investigate + tighten targeting + review copy/CTA
  - > 0.12% = pause send to impacted cohort; require explicit mitigation plan
- Unsubscribe rate:
  - > 1.2% sustained (2+ sends) = messaging/targeting review (not necessarily a hard stop)
- Delivery lag (vendor accepted → delivered):
  - > 30 min p95 for lifecycle sends = check throttles / reputation / vendor issues
- “Not receiving onboarding emails” tickets:
  - ≥ 5 tickets/week or any obvious pattern by region/domain = investigate deliverability + trigger logic

Data we check (minimum cadence)
- Per-send: delivered, hard bounces, soft bounces, blocks, complaints, unsubscribes, unique opens/clicks
- By domain: gmail.com, outlook.com/hotmail.com, yahoo.com + top B2B domains
- By cohort: new signups vs stalled users vs first-success users
- By template: E1 (welcome), E2 (first request), E3 (streaming + examples), E4 (usage dashboard)

Risk log (most recent entries at top)

[2026-02-04] Risk: Spam complaints increased in “stalled users” segment
- Signal(s): complaint rate 0.11% on stalled-user resend (above 0.08% guardrail); unsub rate 1.4%; open rate also down ~3–4 pts vs prior week
- Suspected cause(s): targeting too broad (includes users who already opted out at provider-level), resend window too aggressive (sent within 48h of prior lifecycle touch)
- Severity: High
- Owner: Tyler
- Status: Mitigating (in progress)
- Actions taken:
  - Implemented suppression: no resend within 96h of any lifecycle email (Ethan)
  - Reduced stalled cohort to “no API key + no first request + no docs click” (tighten intent)
  - Asked Soojin to review subject line + preheader for spamminess (avoid “free credits” phrasing)
- Next check: 2026-02-06 (after next stalled cohort send)

[2026-02-02] Risk: “Not receiving onboarding emails” support tickets rising
- Signal(s): SUP-24871 started showing cluster of reports; mostly gmail + a few corporate domains; users confirm they can receive product emails otherwise
- Suspected cause(s): mixture of (a) deliverability (spam/promotions), (b) triggers not firing due to eventing discrepancy / dedupe changes, (c) users signing up with plus-addressing and later searching wrong inbox
- Severity: Medium
- Owner: Ben Carter
- Status: Investigating
- Actions taken:
  - Added support macro: ask user to check Promotions/Spam, verify email address on account, and ensure they didn’t unsubscribe
  - Tyler pulled SendGrid event logs for 20 affected users (delivered vs dropped vs bounced)
  - Ethan verifying trigger logic after event dedupe patch (ensure “signup_completed” is still recorded once)
- Next check: 2026-02-05 (send summary to Support + Growth)

[2026-01-30] Risk: Domain reputation volatility during ramp
- Signal(s): delivered% dipped on Outlook (~1.6% blocked), Gmail remained stable; delivery lag p95 ~22 minutes (higher than normal)
- Suspected cause(s): ramp too fast on new template + low historical volume on subdomain; Outlook more sensitive to template/link patterns
- Severity: Medium
- Owner: Tyler
- Status: Mitigated
- Actions taken:
  - Slowed ramp: cap daily lifecycle volume at 12k/day for 5 days
  - Staggered sends by cohort (new signups first, stalled later)
  - Simplified link set: reduce to 1 primary CTA + 1 secondary (docs) to avoid link reputation issues
- Next check: 2026-02-03 (review Outlook domain stats)

[2026-01-27] Risk: DKIM/SPF/DMARC alignment not consistent across sending paths
- Signal(s): internal checklist flagged potential mismatch between marketing subdomain + envelope-from; deliverability vendor noted alignment could impact Microsoft inboxing
- Suspected cause(s): multiple sending identities; recent config change for lifecycle sends
- Severity: High
- Owner: Tyler
- Status: Mitigated (pending verification)
- Actions taken:
  - INT-3301 created to validate DNS records + alignment end-to-end
  - Confirmed DKIM signing enabled for lifecycle stream; ensured SPF includes vendor IPs
  - Added DMARC policy review step (keep at “p=none” during ramp; revisit later)
- Next check: 2026-02-07 (post-change monitoring; consider moving to stricter DMARC once stable)

[2026-01-24] Risk: Hard bounce spike on first broad send
- Signal(s): hard bounce 1.3% on first larger send (above 1.0% investigate threshold); some “user unknown” at corporate domains
- Suspected cause(s): list quality (invalid emails from self-serve signups), typos, disposable domains
- Severity: Medium
- Owner: Tyler
- Status: Mitigated
- Actions taken:
  - Enabled stricter email validation at signup (lightweight) + flagged disposable domains for additional verification (Ethan to coordinate)
  - Implemented bounce-based suppression: suppress after 1 hard bounce; suppress after 3 soft bounces in 7 days
  - Segmented ramp: new signups only; paused any “stalled user” backfill until bounce normalized
- Next check: 2026-01-31

[2026-01-21] Risk: Template changes increasing spam score
- Signal(s): deliverability vendor flagged certain words in subject/preheader; internal preview showed heavy image-to-text in one variant
- Suspected cause(s): design refresh (DES-311) + copy variants pushing “fastest, cheapest” claims; link density too high
- Severity: Medium
- Owner: Soojin Lee
- Status: Mitigated
- Actions taken:
  - Adjusted language to approved messaging: emphasize reliability/latency transparency, avoid excessive “free/guarantee” language
  - Reduced images; ensured plain-text fallback is clean
  - Added physical address + preference center link consistently
- Next check: ongoing per send

Operational checklist (keep current)
- Before expanding volume:
  - Confirm complaint rate < 0.08% and hard bounce < 1.0% over last 2 sends
  - Confirm unsubscribe link + preference center working (ENG-10518 / PR-28505)
  - Confirm suppression rules: active users (already activated) excluded from “stalled” sends
  - Confirm UTM conventions stable (avoid template changes mid-measurement window)
- Weekly:
  - Review top blocking domains and template-level issues
  - Review support ticket volume (SUP-24871) + any patterns
  - Share a 1-page summary in #marketing (signals + decisions)

Open questions / TODO
- Should we move DMARC from p=none → p=quarantine once ramp stabilizes? (Tyler + Michael)
- Do we need double opt-in for certain geos/segments, or is current consent language sufficient? (Olga + Michael)
- Should “stalled user” segment require an in-product action (e.g., visited docs/console) to reduce cold-email feeling? (Ben + Marissa)

Notes to self (Tyler)
- Biggest recurring failure mode: we treat “stalled” users like marketing list instead of product onboarding. Keep it narrow, helpful, and spaced out.
- If complaint spikes again: pause stalled sends first; don’t touch new signup welcome unless it’s clearly implicated.
